newsitem.title: UK: Crude tanker rates flat, VLCCs to Japan stay firm.
newsitem.headline: Crude tanker rates flat, VLCCs to Japan stay firm.

text.p: Crude oil tanker chartering rates were mostly flat on Thursday and three 255,000 tonne VLCCs (Very Large Crude Carriers) were seen fixed at a healthy W87.5 and W89.75 for Mideast/Japan voyages.
These levels compare to under W50 just three months ago. Similarly-sized vessels carrying Middle Eastern Crude to Singapore were chartered at a buoyant W82.5.

Rates for 80,000 tonners moving within the UK/Cont region held on to recent gains. The fixture of the 80,000 tonne Nordic Torinita at W102.5-W105 was seen below the market and prompt fixtures for these sizes and routes were talked closer to W110-W120.

Chartering of 130,000 tonne Suezmaxes in the Med was heard to have quietened down a little, although rates remained up in the mid-W90s, while West African rates for Suezmaxes sailing to the U.S. were perhaps a little stronger again, as evidenced by the fixture of a 130,000 tonne vessel for mid-September loading at around W98.75.

Fuel oil rates in northwest Europe were talked at around W200-W205 for 25,000 tonne vessels. One 53,000 tonne tanker was seen to have been chartered from northwest Europe to the Med at a rate of W145.
Brokers said this was slightly below the market and pegged rates for 50,000 tonners on these routes at around W165.
